venue: San Francisco Bay Area Stadium, Santa Clara

analysis.summary: A virtual Group D elimination match: both Türkiye and Paraguay lost their openers (Turkey 0-2 to Australia, Paraguay 1-4 to USA) and sit on zero points, meaning the loser is almost certainly eliminated. Turkey hold the clearer squad quality edge with Calhanoglu, Guler and a returning Yildiz, but must improve on a passive first-match display. Paraguay, despite their heavy defeat to the USA, showed resilience and a counter-attacking threat through Julio Enciso and were arguably flattered by the scoreline against the host nation on home soil.
analysis.home_form: Turkey lost 0-2 to Australia on June 14 in Vancouver in their World Cup opener — a counterattacking masterclass by Australia exposed defensive disorganisation. In qualification, Turkey won their European playoff comfortably to reach a first World Cup since 2002. Key players Calhanoglu, Yildiz and Kadioglu all came through the Australia match fit. Yildiz (calf) was restricted to a 45-minute cameo off the bench vs Australia but is reported to be training fully and expected to start or feature heavily. No Turkey players suspended.
analysis.away_form: Paraguay lost 1-4 to USA on June 12 in their opener, with Damian Bobadilla scoring an own goal before halftime and being substituted. Their consolation from Mauricio came at 73 minutes. Pre-tournament friendlies were mixed: W vs Mexico (2-1), L vs Japan (2-2 draw), L vs South Korea (0-2), L vs USA (1-2). Almiron carries an injury doubt. Five Paraguay players who received yellow cards in the USA match are on a suspension tightrope. Caballero (muscular) and Sosa (ankle) also have fitness concerns.
analysis.h2h: Turkey and Paraguay have met only once competitively — a 0-0 friendly in June 1995. No meaningful head-to-head record exists. This is their first-ever competitive meeting.
injuries_news: Kenan Yildiz (Turkey) — calf strain; missed Australia start, came on for 45 minutes; reported to be in full training and likely to feature from the start or early in match
Miguel Almiron (Paraguay) — reported injury doubt, fitness not confirmed ahead of June 20 fixture
Gustavo Caballero (Paraguay) — missed USA match with muscular issue, availability unconfirmed
Ramon Sosa (Paraguay) — ankle problem, status unconfirmed
Damian Bobadilla (Paraguay) — own-goal scorer vs USA, substituted halftime, may be dropped from starting XI
Five Paraguay players on yellow card from Matchday 1 — risk of suspension if booked again (Matchday 2)
key_factors: Must-win dynamic for both teams; the loser is effectively eliminated from a group where USA and Australia both sit on 3 points
Turkey hold a clear squad quality advantage on paper: Calhanoglu, Guler and Yildiz vs Paraguay's more limited attacking options with Almiron doubtful
Paraguay's best hope is a defensive block and quick counter-attacks through Enciso; Turkey's attacking midfield must break them down
Paraguay's 5 yellow-carded players create discipline risk — cautious tackling may limit their pressing intensity
Venue is neutral (Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara); no home advantage for either side
Paraguay conceded 4 goals in their opener but were partly undone by an early own goal against a top-quality USMNT; their defensive line is not as disorganised as the scoreline implies
Turkey's defensive frailties vs Australia (2 goals conceded, exploited on the counter) mean Paraguay's counter-attacking style could produce chances
Rest days roughly equal for both teams (6 days each)
